generatedCommentsNodes.comment: `onClose` is typed as Guava's `Action` while the new `onFatalError` is typed as `Runnable`. Both are single-method, no-arg, no-return functional interfaces and are functionally interchangeable. Using two different types for the same conceptual role (a callback with no arguments) adds unnecessary cognitive overhead for readers. Consider using `Action` for both (or `Runnable` for both) for consistency.

The line
```java
listener.onClose(Status.fromThrowable(mock(Errors.NativeIoException.class)), new Metadata());
```
is redundant. The mock `ClientCall.start` `doAnswer` already invokes `onClose` on the wrapped listener (which delegates to this same `listener`). Since `listener` is an empty `ClientCall.Listener<>() {}`, this second call is a no-op, but it misleads a reader into thinking it is the mechanism that triggers the fatal-error path. Removing it (or adding a brief comment explaining it is intentional) would make the test's intent clearer.

review_comment: We could extend this to cover certain status codes, but I wanted to start with something limited enough to not introduce performance regressions.
This is more of a whitebox test than I would have liked, but I didn't find another way to simulate a connection failure. Open to suggestions here to make this more realistic.
